english.html: and beyond all suspicion <sup class="mk" data-key="f">f</sup>. And briefly to resolve all the contrary arguments, it must be considered that the said de Rols, having been persuaded, together with the sisters and the other principal kinsfolk of the said Martin, both by reason of the likeness and of the tokens, that the said du Tilh was truly her husband — she, having her conscience thus informed <sup class="mk" data-key="g">g</sup>, was not bound to give faith or credit to those who said the contrary, especially persons who had no interest in it <sup class="mk" data-key="h">h</sup>; considering singularly the danger in which she was putting herself, the shame she was uncovering of her own deed, and the peril of receiving a greater one if the denunciation had been found calumnious and false <sup class="mk" data-key="i">i</sup>. Which is a reason that comes greatly into consideration, and by which Papinian excuses the woman violated by force, if she has had shame to disclose such a deed at once to her husband <sup class="mk" data-key="k">k</sup>; and the Emperor commands that the reputation of a woman of worth and honour be entirely preserved to her <sup class="mk" data-key="l">l</sup>. By the above there is answered also what is imputed to the said de Rols, of having believed too lightly that the said du Tilh was her husband <sup class="mk" data-key="m">m</sup>. For she did not believe lightly, considering the interval of time of eight years and the absence of the said Martin, the tokens given by this du Tilh, the assurance that the sisters and uncle of the said Martin gave her, the error and opinion of the rest of the inhabitants of Artigat, who had received, held and esteemed him Martin Guerre, and the longing she had to see and recover her husband. Added to which, as St Ambrose says, a man of worth believes easily <sup class="mk" data-key="n">n</sup>, and this facility proceeds only from a goodness and praiseworthy simplicity <sup class="mk" data-key="o">o</sup>; and to punish here the said de Rols without fault <sup class="mk" data-key="p">p</sup> there is no sufficient cause, nor any scandal or bad example, seeing her error and the just reasons she had to adhere to it. The argument from the history of Lot <sup class="mk" data-key="q">q</sup> is of no service here, for Lot was never judged guilty of having had to do with his daughters, inasmuch as he thought he was approaching his wife; but he was only reproved for his drunkenness, which gave the daughters the boldness to approach their father and converse carnally with him <sup class="mk" data-key="r">r</sup>.

notes.gloss: The wife of a soldier who has had no news of him for four years may send to his commander and, after a further year, remarry without penalty. The law Coras discussed at annot-002 {ſ} and annot-010 {f}; here he reads it as freeing the woman "from all punishment and beyond all suspicion".

lines: & hors de tout ſoupçon {f}. Et pour brieuement reſou-
dre tout les argumens contraires, faut conſiderer, que
ſ'eſtant ladite de Rols perſuadee auec les ſœurs, & au-
tres principaux parẽs dudit Martin, tant pour la raiſon
de la ſimilitude, que des enſeignes que ledit du Tilh
eſtoit veritablement ſon mari: elle ayant ainſi ſa con-
ſcience informee {g}, n'eſtoit pas tenue donner foy, ni
croire ceux qui diſoyent le contratre: meſmement les
perſonnes., qui n'y auoyent aucun intereſt {h}. attendu
ſingulierement le danger, auquel elle ſe mettoit, la hõ-
te qu'elle deſcouuroit de ſon faict, & le peril d'en rece-
uoir vne plus grande, ſi la denonciation ſe fuſt trouuee
calomnieuſe & fauſſe {i} Qui eſt vne raiſon qui vient en
conſideration grande,. & par laquelle Papinien excuſe
la femme violee par force, ſi elle a eu erubeſcence de
manifeſter incontinent tel faict à ſon mari {k}. & l'Em-
pereur commande, que la reputation de femme de biẽ
& honneur luy ſoit entierement gardee {l}. Par ce deſſus
eſt auſſi reſpondu, à ce qu'on impute à ladite de Rols,
d'auoir creu trop legerement, que ledit du Tilh eſtoit
ſon mari {m}. Car elle n'a pas creu de legier, cõſideré l'in-
terualle du temps, de huict annees, & l'abſence dudict
Martin, les enſeignes donnees par iceluy du Tilh,
l'aſſeurance que les ſœurs & oncle dudict Martin luy
donnoiẽt, l'erreur, & opinion du reſte de habitans d'Ar-
tigat, qui l'auoyent receu, tenu & eſtimé Martin Guer-
re, & l'enuie qu'elle auoit de voir, & recouurer ſon ma-
ri. Ioint que comme dit S. Ambroiſe, vn hõme de bien,
croit facilement {n}. & cette facilité ne procede que d'v-
ne bonté, & ſimplicité louable {o}. & de punir ici lad. de
Rols ſans coulpe {p}. n'y a ſuffiſante cauſe, ni aucun ſcan-
dale, ni mauuais exemple, veu ſon erreur, & les iuſtes
raiſons qu'elle auoit d'y adherer. L'argumẽt de l'hiſtoi-
re de Loth {q}, ne ſert rien ici, car Loth n'a eſté iugé onc
coulpable d'auoir participé auec ſes fils: d'autant qu'il
penſoit ſ'approcher de ſa femme, mais a eſté ſeulemẽt
reprins de ſon yurongnerie, qui donna hardieſſe aux
filles, de ſ'approcher de leur pere, & conuerſer charnel-
lement auecques luy {r}.
